candidates.original_title: The white standard: Racial bias in leader categorization
candidates.description: Being White is a component of the business leader prototype; leaders are perceived as White more than non-leaders regardless of base rate information
candidates.citation_sentence: This research is a pre-registered replication of [83] seminal work in leadership categorization theory.
candidates.notes: Close replication of RLP1 (Study 1A). The key effect of interviewee role on perceived race was not significant in the primary analysis (p = 0.08) and only significant in one robustness test restricting to participants who passed manipulation checks. candidates.original_title: The white standard: Racial bias in leader categorization
candidates.description: White leaders are evaluated more favorably than non-White leaders when credit for successful organizational performance is attributed to the leader
candidates.citation_sentence: The core contribution of this study was the finding that 'White leaders were evaluated more favorably than non-White leaders, but only when successful organizational performance was attributed to the leader' (Rosette et al., 2008, p. 769).
candidates.notes: Close replication of RLP3 with student sample at a research university (Study 2A). The three-way interaction was not significant (p = 0.07). The key planned contrast for the LCT hypothesis (high-performance/leader attribution) was not significant (p = 0.95). The main effect of race was significant but in the opposite direction (non-White leader rated higher, p = 0.04). [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
